text.title: Portfolio EVM Rollup Method — Worked Example
text.summary: One complete August rollup of a four-project delivery portfolio with a fifth project stale: two fixed-bid rows on milestone EV, one T&M row on physical percent complete, one LOE row kept apart, a strategic weighting printed beside the currency sum, three-period trends, one escalated project with its narrative, the money block and the owner's signature, with a note on each non-obvious value; then the same month as it is usually reported, with what the validator prints and what the executive misses.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: Portfolio `delivery-2026`, data date 2026-08-31, executive review 2026-09-08, owner portfolio:dana. Five projects run week-grain EVM ledgers; zeus-mobile's PM has been on leave and its last ledger entry is 2026-06-30. Dana's policy escalates SPI or CPI below 0.90 or cost variance beyond 10% of BAC, and applies a strategic weight of 1.5 to hermes-billing.

example.title: delivery-2026 rollup, data date 2026-08-31
example.note: zeus-mobile is in `stale_projects` with its 500k BAC because its last entry (2026-06-30) is two months behind the data date, more than one `month`; its June values are not carried forward (r-single-data-date). hermes-billing on `0/100` earns nothing for M4 until acceptance, which is why EV sits at 400k against 500k PV; a percent-complete ledger would have shown it at 90% (r-normalise-contract-types). Every row names `BAC/CPI` as the formula, so atlas-crm's EAC is 1,200,000 / 0.90 = 1,333,333 and its implied margin 1,400,000 - 1,333,333 = 66,667 (r-per-project-table-fields, r-eac-and-margin-in-money). `aggregate.discrete.spi` is 1,990,000 / 2,100,000 = 0.95, not the mean of 0.90, 0.80 and 1.05 (0.92); ops-support (LOE, SPI 1.00 by construction) is summed in `aggregate.loe` and never enters that ratio (r-rollup-sums-currency-not-indices, r-normalise-contract-types). The strategic weight of 1.5 on hermes-billing gives `weighted.spi` 0.93, printed next to the unweighted 0.95 with the policy document named (r-weighting-policy-declared). Only hermes-billing (SPI 0.80, CPI 0.80, CV 12.5% of BAC) is beyond the 0.90 / 0.90 / 10% thresholds, so it alone carries a narrative and alone appears in `escalated_projects`; atlas-crm at exactly 0.90 is inside (r-variance-thresholds-named). Three trend points per row and for the aggregate show atlas-crm sliding 0.96, 0.92, 0.90 while orion-platform holds above 1.0 (r-trend-three-periods). The money block puts the portfolio 258k over BAC and the two fixed-bid contracts at a combined -33k margin, which is the headline for the review (r-eac-and-margin-in-money). Dana signs on 2026-09-04, four days before the review.

section.title: The same month as it is usually reported

example.title: averaged, snapshot, percent-complete rollup
example.note: What the validator prints: atlas-crm is `fixed-bid` on `physical-percent-complete`, not one of milestone-weight / 0/100 / 50/50 (r-normalise-contract-types); every `trend[]` has 1 point, minimum 3 (r-trend-three-periods); `weighting.policy` is `strategic` with no `policy_document` (r-weighting-policy-declared). Once those are fixed the cross-field checks fire next: zeus-mobile's `data_date` 2026-06-30 differs from the artefact's 2026-08-31 and its ledger is two months old, so it belongs in `stale_projects` (r-single-data-date); `aggregate.discrete.spi` 1.20 is the mean of 1.80, 0.80 and 1.00, while sum(EV) / sum(PV) is 1,680,000 / 1,300,000 = 1.29 (r-rollup-sums-currency-not-indices); hermes-billing is beyond every threshold and has no `variance_narrative`, and `escalated_projects` is empty (r-variance-thresholds-named). What the executive sees: a portfolio 333k under budget with 633k of fixed-bid margin, built on a self-reported 90% complete for atlas-crm and June's numbers for zeus-mobile, while the 100k margin loss on hermes-billing has no cause and no corrective action attached (fm-01, fm-02, fm-03, fm-05, fm-06).
